{{Short description|Ryukyuan record-keeping system}}
{{italic title}}
[[File:Warazan, straw calculator from Ryukyu Islands - Ridai Museum of Modern Science, Tokyo - DSC07450.JPG|thumb|right|250px|Example of ''warazan'' at the Museum of Science, [[Tokyo University of Science]]]]
[[File:"Warazan" 「わら算」Yaeyamajima Kuramoto Kujichō (University of the Ryukyus Library).jpg|thumb|right|250px|Instruction to use ''warazan'' to record the level of tax assessed, in the ''Yaeyama-jima Kuramoto Kujichō'' (1873 copy of the 1857 original); the fourth to sixth characters in the fifth line from the right read「わら算」([[University of the Ryukyus]] Library)<ref name="Komonjo">{{cite web |url=https://www.lib.u-ryukyu.ac.jp/lib_uploadfile/column/h2911_eng.pdf |title=The mathematics from Komonjo |publisher=[[University of the Ryukyus]] Library |date=November 2017 |access-date=31 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://shimuchi.lib.u-ryukyu.ac.jp/collection/miyara/mi00501/13 |script-title=ja:八重山島蔵元公事帳 |trans-title=Administrative Guidelines Of Yaeyama Kuramoto |language=ja |publisher=[[University of the Ryukyus]] Library |access-date=31 August 2021}}</ref>]]
{{nihongo|'''''Warazan'''''|藁算}} was a system of record-keeping using knotted straw at the time of the [[Ryukyu Kingdom|Ryūkyū Kingdom]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.l.u-tokyo.ac.jp/postgraduate/database/2015/165.html |script-title=ja:沖縄諸島の土着書記体系の研究 |title=Native Writing Systems in the Okinawan Islands |language=ja, en |publisher=[[University of Tokyo]] |year=2015 |access-date=31 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://older.minpaku.ac.jp/english/research/activity/project/iurp/07jr100 |title=A Study of Ryukyu Materials in the Collection of the National Museum of Ethnology |author=Sasaki Toshikazu |publisher=[[National Museum of Ethnology (Japan)|National Museum of Ethnology]] |access-date=31 August 2021}}</ref> In the [[Southern Ryukyuan languages]] of the [[Sakishima Islands]] it was known as ''barazan'' and on [[Okinawa Island]] as ''warazani'' or ''warazai''.<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www2.tsuda.ac.jp/suukeiken/math/suugakushi/sympo25/25_17miyata.pdf |script-title=ja:古代中国における計算の起源 |trans-title=The Origins of Reckoning in Ancient China |language=ja |author=Miyata Yoshimi 宮田義美 |journal=Reports of Institute for Mathematics and Computer Science, Tsuda University|publisher=[[Tsuda University]] |date=27 December 2014 |page=358}}</ref> Formerly used in particular in relation to the "head tax", it is still to be found in connection with the annual {{nihongo|Itoman Giant Tug-of-War|糸満大綱引}}, to record the amount of ''miki'' or sacred ''[[sake]]'' dedicated.<ref name="Komonjo"/>
